- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer below forecast for volatility.
- When official events are frequent (≥15 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast growth by 10–20% relative to baseline.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation), model may misread trend; use moving average of last 5 sentiment values to adjust forecast direction.
- For short-term (1–3 day) forecasts, model often lags sentiment shifts; align forecast with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is rising.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “overbought” bias.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 1–2% downward adjustment to prevent false momentum.
